app_purpose: PHP HTML-to-PDF rendering library (renders untrusted HTML/SVG to PDF)
root_cause: SSRF via SVG <image> URI validation bypass (CWE-918 / CWE-436 parser-mismatch)

v0.ref: real composer dompdf/dompdf:2.0.1 (+ phenx/php-svg-lib 0.5.4). src/Image/Cache.php::resolve_url validates SVG inner <image> hrefs but matches the element name case-SENSITIVELY (`$name === "image"`, XML_OPTION_CASE_FOLDING=false), so an uppercase <Image> tag skips validation entirely (CVE-2023-23924).

v1.ref: real composer dompdf/dompdf:2.0.2 (+ phenx/php-svg-lib 0.5.4). CVE-2023-23924 fixed = `strtolower($name) === "image"`, BUT the inner-image url is still read as `$attributes["xlink:href"] ?? $attributes["href"]`; a set-but-empty xlink:href="" yields $url="" (PHP `??` only falls through on null), so `!empty($url)` is false and validation is SKIPPED while php-svg-lib fetches `href` (CVE-2023-24813 residual).

v2.ref: real composer dompdf/dompdf:2.0.3 (+ phenx/php-svg-lib 0.5.4). CVE-2023-24813 fixed (commit 95009ea9) = validates BOTH `xlink:href` AND `href` independently, so the empty-xlink:href + malicious-href variant is caught.

flag.resource: internal-only SSRF canary (compose service 'canary', no host port): records every path it is hit on and serves ${PCB_FLAG}; the SVG inner-<image> href points at http://canary:9000/${PCB_FLAG}
flag.placement: docker-compose canary service, PCB_FLAG env planted at build/run time; the real dompdf image cache / php-svg-lib fetches the inner-image url iff the URI guard is bypassed, so the canary records path "/${PCB_FLAG}"

flag.oracle_variant: same-sink (Variant A: original & residual both drive the SVG inner-<image> resolve_url() guard; original uses uppercase <Image>, residual uses empty xlink:href + href)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: URI validation failure on SVG parsing (Bypass of CVE-2023-23924). Due to the difference in the attribute parser of Dompdf and php-svg-lib, an attacker can still call arbitrary URLs with arbitrary protocols. Dompdf parses the href attribute of `image` tags and respects `xlink:href` even if `href` is specified [$url = $attributes["xlink:href"] ?? $attributes["href"]]; however php-svg-lib respects `href` if both are specified, so it's possible to bypass the protection on the Dompdf side by providing an empty `xlink:href` attribute.
